evidence.excerpt:
## Problem

Data warehouse incremental syncs OOM the import workers during the Delta merge, and the existing auto-repartition controller misses several cases.
Three gaps.
The size budget is measured in compressed at-rest bytes, but the merge's memory is the decompressed Arrow working set, so tables with wide nested-JSON columns sit "under budget" yet still OOM.
Nothing records which tables actually OOM, so detection can only guess from size.
And tombstone debt builds up on tables that OOM their merge (they never reach the post-load compaction), while a few tables end up with a corrupt `_delta_log` from an interrupted repartition swap and loop forever.

## Changes

- **OOM history.** New `ExternalDataSchemaOOMEvent` model, one row per detected pod heartbeat-timeout, recorded per Temporal retry at the point we already detect the timeout. A dedicated model rather than `sync_type_config` json, because a single job can OOM many times across retries and the json would grow unbounded.
- **Hybrid repartition trigger.** Lowered the at-rest budget from ~1 GB to ~0.5 GB so it leaves headroom for concurrent merges on a shared 29 GB worker (a single OOM kills every co-tenant activity on the pod). Added an OOM-history override so a repeatedly-OOM'd table is repartitioned even when its compressed size looks fine, because its real working set (wide nested-JSON) is bigger than the at-rest size implies.

evidence.title: danielcarletti · material review on #68639
evidence.excerpt:
Rather than having both maintenance triggers write the watermark independently, let's collapse them into a single entry point so the watermark write exists exactly once.

vacuum_table can't own the watermark — it's a DeltaTableHelper method and the watermark lives in schema.sync_type_config, which the helper (correctly) knows nothing about. Instead: add one run_maintenance(partition_count, last_vacuum_version, commit_threshold) -> int | None on the helper that does compact_if_fragmented first and only falls through to vacuum_if_stale when compaction didn't run (compact already vacuums, so it supersedes). It returns the single version-to-persist, and run_pre_write_defensive_compact remains the sole place that writes last_vacuum_version.

This gets us: one decision point, at most one vacuum per run (the fragmented+stale double-vacuum goes away structurally rather than via a short-circuit), one watermark write, and compact_table/vacuum_table keep their current signatures. evidence.title: #70648 · feat(devex): let light worktrees borrow toolchain from main clone
evidence.excerpt:
## Problem

Creating a worktree for a small change is disproportionately heavy. A plain `git worktree add` bootstraps a ~343 MB root pnpm install just so pre-commit hooks can run, and committing any Python file still fails outright because there is no venv for `bin/hogli` (and `uv run` would silently build a full ~2.3 GB `.venv` in the worktree). The alternative, a full flox setup per worktree, costs several GB of node_modules plus flox cache each time. Sharing deps at the package-manager level was tried before with `enableGlobalVirtualStore` (#57452) and reverted the same day (#57638) because it broke Vite dependency resolution and could not be opted out per user.

## Changes

Light worktrees now borrow the main clone's toolchain instead of installing their own, guarded by lockfile equality:

- New `bin/helpers/worktree-borrow.sh`, sourced by the husky hooks. In a linked worktree without local installs it puts the main clone's `.flox/run/*/bin` (pnpm, node, uv), `node_modules/.bin`, and venv on `PATH`, but only while the worktree's `pnpm-lock.yaml` / `uv.lock` are byte-identical to the main clone's. On mismatch it prints what to install and everything falls back to today's behavior. Local installs always win over borrowing.
- `.husky/post-checkout` skips the bootstrap install when borrowing applies. Hooks source the helper relative to the hook file, which works whether git resolves `core.hooksPath` against the main clone (git 2.53 default with husky's relative `.husky`) or per worktree.
- `bin/hogli` gains the main clone's venv as a guarded fallback, so hook commands work

evidence.excerpt:
Stacked on #62672 (base = its branch; will retarget to master once it merges). Greenlit by Julian off a 14-day PR survey.

**What changes:** previews stop being opt-in. - Eligibility lives in a cheap credential-free `decide` job (github-script, no checkout/tailnet/token), not an `on.paths` filter — a path filter would kill the label-only flow for backend PRs.

evidence.excerpt:
## Problem

The cohort processor and the backfill seeder decode the same condition bytecode again on every single evaluation.

- #74117 made `hogvm::Program::from_shared` decode the whole token array, and `CohortEvaluator` called it once per (event, condition) pair.
- One event with several hundred person conditions pays several hundred full decodes.
- A `person.properties.X IN (...)` leaf allocates one `Arc<str>` per string literal, per evaluation. Real catalogs hold lists of thousands of elements.

evidence.title: sinan-ku · material review on #94104
evidence.excerpt:
**Demo data skips the source access check**

`publish_reusable_widget` reads up to 20 rows per input with the publisher's run authorization, and stores them in `GeneratedWidgetVersion.demo_data`. This function returns those rows to any user who has notebook viewer and query viewer access.

The notebook frame endpoint also calls `_require_run_connection_access` (`views/notebook.py:721`). Its comment says: "Notebook + query access does not imply source access." The demo path does not run that check, and it does not check object-level access to the source notebook. As a result, a user who cannot read a warehouse source, or a restricted notebook, can read those rows through the catalog. Restore and generation copy `demo_data` forward, so the rows stay after an edit.

Suggestions:
- Record the connection or source of each captured frame, and check it again here.
- Or store only the schema, with synthetic demo rows.
- At minimum, tell the publisher in the publish modal that sample rows become visible to the team.

Introduces a shared **ProductEmptyState** platform and adopts it for MCP analytics as the reference implementation.

- `ProductEmptyState` + `ProductEmptyStateGate`, driven by a single-layer `productSetupStatusLogic` contract (`loading | needs-setup | waiting-for-data | has-data`). A scene opts in by declaring `emptyState` on its `SceneExport`; detection stays per-product but pushes a normalized status into one place any surface can read.
- Detection must be a real signal (data-existence query / entity count), never a dismissal flag. Skip is local-only (per browser, per team) so the real product appears the moment data lands.
- MCP analytics: in-scene setup screen with the wizard command (`TerminalCard`), a low-fidelity interactive tool-call preview (filter chips + a self-tracing sparkline), a dedicated `--color-product-mcp-analytics-*` accent, and removal of the old redirect-to-onboarding path. **The underlying event-detection query is unchanged from what shipped before** — only the routing around it moved in-scene.
